steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Ai—yah!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Phew... good, good.

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: Are you okay, Warmy?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Hehe, I'm fine! I caught the dish! And look at the bowls! They're all fine!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Sorry, Nanna Radish Leaves. I just got this staff, so I'm not used to it yet, and I sometimes knock things over when I'm not paying attention.
The girl stands on her tiptoes to put the fallen plates and bowls back to where they belong.

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: Haha, silly girl.

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: Remember? Back when you used to come to my place for cystymilk crisps, you needed a little stool to reach your bowl in the cupboard.

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: Come, let Nanna see. You've grown quite tall...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Hehe, I think so too!

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: Let's see. Oh dear, your collar's got a snagged thread.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Oh, you're right... I've been traveling for so long, I haven't even noticed...

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: Come, get changed. I'll patch this up for you.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It's okay, Nanna. I can fix this myself.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Look, I have my own little sewing kit!

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: *sigh*, you must've had it pretty hard on the road.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Didn't you say in the letter that somebody moved into the room I was in?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It feels like... not a lot has changed here.

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: After you'd left, I did have a few young men move in. Haven't you heard that they found a new area rich in minerals in the next town over?

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: Just like you, the kid who stayed here before simply left a letter and took off in a hurry.

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: What's the matter? Have you talked to your Uncle Fat Head about staying here today? Hold on just a moment. I'll get your room ready.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It's okay, Nanna. I'll be leaving again soon.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I'm back here this time because I wanted to see everybody again... including my dad.

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Button Shop Tailor
steps.text: I haven't heard anything about your father lately. Maybe you could try asking around. Somebody might just have heard something.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Yep, it's okay.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: And there's one other really important thing—

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: They'll play an outdoor movie at the rundown factory plot this evening.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Why don't you come?! I'll pay for everyone's tickets!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Huh? Why are you laughing? I really will!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: We actually made it through all kinds of danger and crossed a sandbeast's paradise that nobody knows about, and found a Feranmut nest there!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: There are lots, lots, lots of really tall Originium crystals there... They're even taller than these tower cranes and furnaces!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Hah, good! I believe you!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: I'll tell all the workers how you visited that Blinking Valley place far, far away...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It's the Grinning Valley!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Ah, right. The Grinning Valley!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: You've been traveling for so long, Warmy. I'm sure you've picked up plenty of new skills.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: But you know, I think it's good enough as long as you stay safe out there.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Remember to come back and visit more often.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Mm, but I...

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Look at this. What did I just tell you?

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: I said I'd make this thing as good as new before you finished telling two stories, didn't I?

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Now take this folding chair back to your nanna Radish Leaves! Tell her she could tap dance on the chair and it wouldn't break!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Okay! Thanks, Uncle Mustache!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: And also...

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Hm? What else do you need?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: There's gonna be an outdoor movie screening this evening... Let's watch together!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Outdoor movie? Hah, no wonder she wanted to get this folding chair fixed.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Alright, then. I'll go!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: It's been years since the last time I watched a movie. All they've been playing are those adventure flicks. That's what young people these days like, no?

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Old folks like us prefer those slow-paced family films.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Not at all. I love family movies.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Back then... It was Daddy who asked me to watch movies with him.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I still remember how he would tear up whenever the relatives said goodbye to the main characters with smiles on their faces...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: That's even though he was a grown man.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Your old man... right.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: He's a sentimental one. We all know it.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: My kid—you know the one you called Screwhead—he went to the cities to study engineering.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: I couldn't leave for too long, because of my business. It was your old man who took him to school whenever it was time to go back... Remember?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Yep, I remember.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: When I was small, every time he left for work, he'd bring me to your shop.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Even though he told me he was going to the mines, I always asked you where he was...

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Haha, that's right.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: You've always got on so well with your old man. *sigh* You really miss him, don't you?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I heard Screwhead's graduated, stayed in the city, and even got a good job.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I'm so glad!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: And I know my daddy would be really happy, too!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Good kid...

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Right... right. Your old man definitely knows. He doesn't talk much, but news always gets to him fast.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: He's probably working in some mine right now, with a lot of weight on his shoulders... I'm sure of it! I just hope their card games there aren't much different from here.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: I know when you two see each other again, he'll be very proud of what a big girl you've become!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Right, that big mining ship you're off to. Where's it headed?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Hm... I'm not really sure.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Lanns and Savage told me that I'm going to Rhodes Island to get treatm—No, that's not all. It's so I can learn lots and lots of new things!

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Alright, but promise me this. Take care of yourself, okay?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Yep... I will!

steps.name: Construction Team Bricklayer
steps.text: Hey, Ol' Mustache! Here's your loudspeaker.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Alright, got it!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Loudspeaker?

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Haha, you've never seen such a strange looking trinket? It's one of the hottest products developed by Screwhead's company.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Kid tells me it's got such a narrow, crooked neck because that's how it carries sound to far-off places.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Well, the workers here just use it to chitchat up on the scaffolding... but that ain't so bad, right?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Uncle Mustache.

steps.name: Repair Shop Machinist
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Is it okay if I borrow this?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Hello, everybody... Huh?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) Hello, everybody!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Whoa... Why is it so loud...?
The workers, all dressed in a variety of outfits, look to the source of the sound.
They see a young girl with a loudspeaker poking her head through the rusted shutters.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) Hello, everybody! Tonight...!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) Tonight, let's watch an outdoor movie together!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) At the same place as before, the rundown factory plot!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) A-And also...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) Remember not too eat too much for dinner. I'll have snacks for everyone!

steps.name: Factory Inventory Keeper
steps.text: Huh? There's a movie today? And snacks?

steps.name: Factory Quality Checker
steps.text: Just the thing I need after spending all night inspecting galvanized steel!

steps.name: Factory Quality Checker
steps.text: Hey, lads, don't forget to grab a couple cases of fizzy drinks from the canteen!

steps.name: Factory Procurement Worker
steps.text: Right, whose kid was that again? She's got a loud voice.

steps.name: Factory Auditor
steps.text: I remember her... From the looks of it, she must've found her old man. Good. Good...

steps.name: Factory Porter
steps.text: Oh, so that's her... How long has she been gone? Two years? So it's been two years already...?

steps.name: Factory Porter
steps.text: Ah... two years, in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Factory Technician
steps.text: Heh, it's like the blink of an eye to us alright.

steps.name: Factory Technician
steps.text: But I'm sure those same two years have been a very long time to her.
The factory workers keep piling into the empty plot.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) Everyone! The movie is about the start!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) If you have tall chairs, lean back as much as you can. If you have short ones, come as close to the front as possible to not block the people behind!
There are rows and rows of seats. Most have already taken settled in, while a few are trying to find a spot more to their liking.
Some run up to the roof, some decide to dangle themselves from a crane, and some opt just to go to behind the silver screen.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: (Loudspeaker) Potlid—

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: H-Hu-Huh?! Lanns?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Oh no! I haven't turned the loudspeaker off yet!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Huh? Loudspeaker?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: So everyone here heard my nickname for you loud and clear, then?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: How about it? Everyone thinks it's a great nickname, right?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: *whimper*...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hello? Can anyone hear me?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I'm never speaking to you again!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Alright, alright. I'm sorry... I'm just worried about you!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Didn't we agree you'd reach out to me as soon as you finished saying hi to the townspeople?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Oh, right.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I got so busy that I forgot...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What do I do with you...? Never mind. Are you happy you got to see everyone?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Yep, I'm very happy!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Really, really happy!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Haha, that's good. Very good.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Warmy, the movie is about to start!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Oh, coming!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Now off you go.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Finish saying all the things you've been holding in for the last couple years. We'll come to the town's station to pick you up tomorrow.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Lanns, I can go tonight.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But... Would it be alright to have you pick me up there?
The workers keep their eyes focused on the screen. The protagonist's monologue is echoing in their ears.

a.text: 'At the time, I still didn't know where that truck would take him.'
'The wilderness is vast. If you get separated, you may never see each other again.'
'But where is the path ahead that I seek?'
'Having missed the last ride, I follow the dark road and march onward to daybreak.'

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Huh...? Is the movie over already?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But it kind of feels like the story's not over yet... What did the main character mean by that in the end?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I don't think I get it... but everyone must've really enjoyed the movie...

steps.name: Broadcast Station Clerk
steps.text: Ah, good movie.

steps.name: Broadcast Station Clerk
steps.text: I'm jealous... He spent a lifetime chasing a single idea. So courageous.

steps.name: Furniture Factory Woodworker
steps.text: Oh, please. This stuff only ever happens in movies. Nobody would be so unrealistic in real life.

steps.name: Furniture Factory Woodworker
steps.text: Take a guess. Why didn't the director give us a clear conclusion to his story?

steps.name: Furniture Factory Woodworker
steps.text: Everybody knows it in their hearts. He's walking into the mountains, the valleys, to the ends of the earth... He's just walking to a dead end.

steps.name: Broadcast Station Clerk
steps.text: A dead end?

steps.name: Broadcast Station Clerk
steps.text: You son of a mother... How could you say that?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Hm... I remember these two always bickering with each other...)

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (I'm getting a bad feeling about this...)

steps.name: Broadcast Station Clerk
steps.text: They made the ending like this because they wanted us to fill in the rest ourselves. You can't figure even that out?

steps.name: Broadcast Station Clerk
steps.text: If you see nothing but a dead end ahead of him, then I can only feel sorry for how life's been treating you!

steps.name: Furniture Factory Woodworker
steps.text: Hmph, I saw an irresponsible man and that's all. Maybe you're like him.

steps.name: Furniture Factory Woodworker
steps.text: If my kid grows up to be like him, I'll beat him 'till he can't leave town!

steps.name: Broadcast Station Clerk
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Furniture Factory Woodworker
steps.text: What? Wanna go? Let's do it!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Wh-Why are they fighting all of a sudden?!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Stop fighting—

steps.name: Spectating Worker
steps.text: Heh! I knew we'd be treated to a wrestling match after the movie!

steps.name: Spectating Worker
steps.text: Yeah, hold him down! Don't let him fight back!

steps.name: Spectating Worker
steps.text: Quick, pass out the drinks I brought with me. It's time for the encore!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Wait... It wasn't supposed to go like this...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: After the movie, it should've been...

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Quit making trouble!

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Hyah!

steps.name: Broadcast Station Clerk
steps.text: Ugh... my arm...

steps.name: Furniture Factory Woodworker
steps.text: Eek... My back...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Wow, that's amazing... You stopped the two of them in one go!

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: *sigh*... You came back for a visit after so long, and these morons didn't change for even one bit.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: It's all okay... Everyone's always yelled at each other for as long as I can remember... Although today feels especially bad.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Good thing you're still here, Uncle Fat Head. You took care of them so quickly.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Not just me. Your desserts helped, too.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Help me put the tape back in the cabinet by the wall, Warmy.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: N-Nothing! I was just looking at how long the case says the movie is.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: So that was actually the full version...

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Haha... Sounds like you don't like the movie's ending, either.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: N-Not at all. I really like it.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: The movie doesn't say... but I think the main character has already reached his goal and is ready to start a new journey.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Oh, that's just what I think... Even if everyone ends up fighting over what they think the ending is about... I think everyone's opinions are valid!

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Silly girl... Why does it matter what anyone else thinks? What's important is what you think.

spans.text: Silly girl... Why does it matter what anyone else thinks? What's important is what

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: So why did you want to show a movie today, Warmy?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I just wanted to get everyone together to have some fun... just like what Daddy used to do...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Every time he left home, he'd watch a movie with everybody.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: He said... That's how you cheer everyone up.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Warmy... You're all grown up now.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: I can tell... You wanted to say a proper goodbye, right?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But things got so out of hand, I didn't get a chance...

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: But, you know what? You've already said your goodbye.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: When you invited all of us here, you told us what you've been through the last two years.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: We can tell you've been taking care of yourself and made new friends... We all know. Just like the movie's main character, you've started a new journey.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: The most important thing is you're still young. You have all kinds of possibilities open to you. Do what it is that you want to do.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: It doesn't matter if you want to stay here, keep looking for your old man, or something else...

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: All of us will support you.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Uncle Fat Head...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: Silly girl. What's there to thank?

steps.name: Town Projectionist
steps.text: The next time you're back, we'll watch another movie together. How does that sound?

steps.name: Mineral Transport Worker
steps.text: Here we are, girl.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Mineral Transport Worker
steps.text: You see the transport station up ahead? I hear they stopped running the last route to here not too long ago. Good thing the station hasn't been torn down, and the lights are still up.

steps.name: Mineral Transport Worker
steps.text: I've got cargo to deliver, so I can't stay with you. Be careful out there.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Thanks for the ride.

steps.name: Mineral Transport Worker
steps.text: Don't mention it.

steps.name: Mineral Transport Worker
steps.text: There are lots of rocks on the road here. Be careful and don't trip.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I will!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Don't worry. I've walked this path many, many times before.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I won't fall down again.
The girl stops walking.
Ahead, the abandoned tracks are engulfed by the intense darkness. On the ground, a mining hard hat with a large conspicuous dent and a bent, misshapen valve handwheel lie forgotten.
A mining lamp on the ground flickers repeatedly before suddenly losing its glimmer.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I miss you.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But... I'm going somewhere far, far away now.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Lanns says we're going even farther away than the transports go, and the Grinning Valley...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: B-But you don't have to worry about me... Everyone'll be waiting for Warmy...
The young girl crosses into the loosely cordoned off area and walks toward the ruins.
She strokes the ice-cold surface of a rock, as though reminiscing that large, rough hand that she never once thought she would ever take her hand off.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Daddy...

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Bye bye.
